chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Ayoub ibn Al-Hurr, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The wage of the female singer who attends the weddings is not problematic, provided she is not the one whom men enter upon (for private entertainment).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible
key_terms.يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهَا الرِّجَالُ: Men enter upon her (implies private or specific entertainment context)

ai.seo_question: Is the income of a female wedding singer permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling in *al-Kafi* to distinguish between permissible wedding entertainment and the broader prohibition of *istihlal* (making lawful what is forbidden) often associated with female singers in pre-Islamic and early Islamic contexts. The condition 'not the one entered upon by men' (*laysat bi-allati yadkhulu alayha al-rijal*) is interpreted by Shia jurists as ensuring modesty and preventing the specific context of *khala'ah* (seclusion) or mixed-gender intimacy that invalidates the earnings. This highlights the Shia emphasis on contextual permissibility (*al-ibahah al-muqayyadah*) rather than a blanket prohibition on female vocal performance.
